title: Applying Interval Arithmetic Techniques to Formal Verification of Floating-Point AI Safety Properties

original_idea.body:
# Applying Interval Arithmetic Techniques to Formal Verification of Floating-Point AI Safety Properties

**Problem:** Floating-point arithmetic is notoriously non-associative and error-prone. AI models use floating-point extensively. Interval arithmetic (a formal method for bounding floating-point errors) could be applied to formally verify safety properties of AI computation, but this transfer has not been made.

**Direction:** Select 5 simple neural network computations (softmax, attention score, normalization). Use Lean 4 or Coq with interval arithmetic libraries to formally bound the floating-point error. Measure whether LLMs can generate these proofs with appropriate numeric bounds. Assess what safety properties can be guaranteed.

**Why it matters:** If formal interval arithmetic can bound AI computation errors, it provides a rigorous foundation for AI safety properties related to numerical stability. This bridges floating-point formal methods and AI safety.

**Relevant context:** Coq's Flocq library and Lean's Float library support formal floating-point reasoning. Interval arithmetic is used in scientific computing verification. No work applies it to AI model computation verification.
